pages.text: One windy afternoon, <name> ran to the park with a bright, red kite. As he held the string, the kite suddenly wiggled and squeaked, “Hello, <name>! Want to hear a joke?”

<name> blinked. “A talking kite? Really?” “Yes! Why did the cloud bring a suitcase?” the kite giggled. “I… don’t know,” said <name>. “Because it was going on a rainy vacation!” the kite laughed, spinning in the sky.

Excited, <name> let the kite soar higher. Suddenly, it looped and twirled, forming funny shapes—a giant spiral, a zig-zag, and even a smiley face. Other kites nearby floated closer, joining the magical kite party.

“Come on, friends! Let’s make shapes!” the talking kite called. Soon, the sky was filled with laughing kites, twisting and twirling in rainbow patterns. <name> ran under them, giggling as a kite looped near his head and shouted, “Duck, silly human!”

At one point, the kite flew a little too high. <name> tugged carefully, and it came back down, wobbling like it was laughing. The friends joined him, each flying kites while the talking kite told more jokes, making everyone laugh.
By evening, <name> sat in the grass, smiling and catching his breath. The kite hovered gently, wiggling happily. “Best kite day ever!” <name> said, amazed at the magical, giggling adventure.
